results.title: 8% pay rise: Workers will be better off in real terms— Dr Acheampong
results.content: Workers in the public sector are expected to be better off in real terms than they were in several previous years, as easing inflation helps preserve the purchasing power of their salaries, Technical Adviser at the Ministry of Finance, Dr Theo Acheampong, has said.

results.title: UK and EU agree draft deal to scrap Brexit red tape over food exports
results.content: The UK and EU have agreed a draft deal to remove post-Brexit checks on food and agricultural exports, ahead of the UK-EU summit later this month.

results.title: North Korea denies being behind record $6.3bn Binance hack
results.content: North Korea has denied claims that it was behind the record $6.3bn (£4.7bn) hack of cryptocurrency exchange Binance, calling the allegations "absurd rhetoric".

results.title: Chief of Staff urges African leaders to see diaspora citizens beyond remittances
results.content: “We must see the diaspora beyond the form of support and remittances to our families. Diaspora can create businesses; Diaspora can create trade channels and businesses that will support economic growth across the continent. We commend the work of Elevate Africa in championing the African dream”.

results.title: 8% pay rise: We’ll reopen negotiations if economic conditions worsen – NAGRAT warns
results.content: The President of the National Association of Graduate Teachers (NAGRAT), Jacob Anaba, says organised labour may return to the negotiating table over the eight per cent base pay increase for public sector workers in 2027 if economic conditions change during the year.

results.title: Beyond survival: The unseen battles breast cancer survivors continue to fight
results.content: Every October, breast cancer awareness campaigns remind us of the importance of early detection, prevention and access to treatment. Advocates call on governments to equip health facilities, strengthen cancer services and ensure that patients receive timely care. These demands are necessary. In Ghana, delays in accessing treatment remain a concern, with a 2025 study of patients referred for breast biopsies in the Oti and Volta regions documenting substantial gaps in treatment initiation.

results.title: T-bills auction: Government borrowed GH¢14bn in October 2026
results.content: Last week, investor appetite for T-bills moderated at October’s final auction, with total bids declining by 40.28% week-on-week to GH¢2.55bn.

results.title: Bond market: Turnover declined by 44% to GH¢5.03bn

results.title: NAGRAT demands minimum and maximum base pay to address wage inequality
results.content: The President of the National Association of Graduate Teachers (NAGRAT), Jacob Anaba, has called for a review of the public sector salary adjustment system, proposing minimum and maximum base pay levels to address what he describes as wide inequalities in workers’ earnings.

results.title: Kotoka Airport remains legal name until Parliament passes renaming Bill – A-G
results.content: The Attorney-General has told the Supreme Court that Kotoka International Airport remains the facility's legal name, as the legislative process to rename it Accra International Airport has not yet been completed. The suit was filed by Austin Kwabena Brako-Powers, who is seeking a declaration that the government's decision to rename Kotoka International Airport without first amending NLCD 339 is unconstitutional. The plaintiff's case centres on whether the proposed change can lawfully proceed while the decree establishing the General Kotoka Trust remains in force. The Attorney-General maintains that the decree remains operative and that the proposed renaming must go through Parliament before it can take legal effect. results.title: Workers still struggle to make ends meet despite low inflation — NAGRAT President
results.content: Workers continue to struggle to make ends meet despite easing economic indicators, the President of the National Association of Graduate Teachers (NAGRAT), Jacob Anaba, has said, warning that the agreed eight per cent increase in base pay for public sector workers in 2027 will offer limited relief if prices of goods and services continue to rise.

results.title: Daily Insight for CEOs: The CEO’s Role in Driving Year-End Performance
results.content: November marks a critical stage in the organisation’s performance journey. With only two months remaining in 2026, CEOs must intensify their focus on delivering strategic commitments, closing performance gaps, and ensuring that resources are directed towards the results that matter most. Year-end performance does not improve through pressure alone. It requires clear priorities, timely decisions, executive ownership, and consistent monitoring of progress.

results.title: Russian bombing kills 26 people at Ukraine aid centre, Kyiv says
results.content: At least 26 people were killed after Russian bombs hit an aid distribution centre, in an attack that Ukraine's leader has called "utterly horrific".

results.title: Copilot in deadly Florida jet crash identified in reports as 20-year-old
results.content: A 20-year-old copilot was among nine people killed when a small jet crashed and exploded in Florida on Sunday, according to US media.

results.title: Man guilty of stealing cash from farm owned by South African president
results.content: A court in South Africa has found a man guilty of stealing more than $500,000 (£372,822) in cash from a farm owned by South African president Cyril Ramaphosa, in a case that mired the head of state in an impeachment saga.

results.title: No new Ghana Cards required under biometric verification law – NIA
results.content: The National Identification Authority (NIA) has assured Ghanaians that implementing the National Identity Register Amendment Regulation, 2026 (L.I. 2523), does not require new Ghana Cards or fresh biometric registration.

results.title: Sheffield researcher helps shape global policy on school meals and child health
results.content: Dr Robert Akparibo, Senior Lecturer in Global Health and Nutrition at the University of Sheffield, is working with international organisations and researchers to ensure these issues receive the attention they deserve in global policy.
